document_check.note: Document is Yang M, Wang Y, Tian C, et al. 'Development and External Validation of a Gait Test Based Diagnostic Model for Detecting Mild Cognitive Impairment', Arch Phys Med Rehabil 2024;105:930-8. This matches 'Yang et al. 2024, P-604'. The cited AUC 0.906 (dual-task gait model) versus 0.989 (MoCA) and the authors' explanation about the MoCA's role in the diagnostic criteria are both in the document (p7-8).

cited_result: Derivation-sample discrimination of the serial-subtraction-7 dual-task gait model (gait speed, dual-task cost, years of education): AUC 0.906 (95% CI 0.854 to 0.958), compared with AUC 0.989 for a MoCA-only model in the same data (p4, p7, Table 4).
tool_reason: The cited result is the discrimination of a multivariable logistic diagnostic model for MCI and its ranking against a MoCA model, so PROBAST applies.

domains.rationale: The study uses a diagnostic case-control design with convenience sampling. Common gait-affecting conditions (osteoarthritis, frailty, sarcopenia, stroke) and anyone with missing predictor data were excluded, which is inappropriate for a community screening model.

domains.rationale: MCI was diagnosed by specialist physicians using NIA-AA criteria, applied identically in both samples. Gait predictors are not part of the definition. Whether diagnosticians knew the gait results, and the interval between diagnosis and gait testing, are not reported. The MoCA comparator is incorporated into the reference standard.

domains.rationale: There are 62 events for many candidate predictors. Predictors were chosen by forward stepwise selection after univariable screening of gait tests, and the best of three models was picked by AUC in the same data. Participants with missing data were excluded, and there was no resampling-based internal validation; the 'internal validation' was an age and sex subgroup check. The cited AUC 0.906 is therefore apparent performance. The temporal external validation is small (19 MCI cases), and its reported sensitivity and specificity do not match its reported group sizes.

applicability.rationale: The sample is a convenience case-control sample from five Wuhan communities that excluded osteoarthritis, frailty, sarcopenia, stroke and joint surgery. This differs from the unselected older community population in which the model is intended for screening.
The predictors are phone-video gait speed, dual-task cost and education, which are feasible at screening.
MCI is defined by standard NIA-AA clinical criteria.

overall: High risk of bias (PROBAST); high concern for applicability
overall_rationale: Domain 1 is high because of the case-control design, convenience sampling and exclusion of gait-affecting conditions and missing data. Domain 4 is high because of low events per candidate predictor, stepwise and univariable-guided selection, model choice on the same data, complete-case exclusion and no optimism correction. The cited AUC 0.906 is apparent performance. The MoCA comparison is further biased in the MoCA's favour because the MoCA forms part of the reference standard.
